title_as_printed: Solubility of Carbon Dioxide and Nitrous Oxide in Water
pressure_note: gas partial pressure 760 mm of mercury (alpha defined at partial pressure of 760 mm)

value.what: S = alpha / (weight fraction of water x density); for pure water mL gas STP per g water

value2.what: Bunsen coefficient: volume of gas reduced to 0 C and 760 mm Hg dissolved per volume of water at 760 mm partial pressure

uncertainty.unit: printed average deviation x 1000, quantity not named (probably alpha); symbol illegible in the scan

volume_basis_evidence: 'one volume of solvent' (definition of alpha); pure water so solvent = solution
gas_basis_evidence: pure water; no gas mole fractions reported
conversion_needs: alpha or S to molality: S/22414*1000 (ideal-gas), see Table II note on non-ideality
notes: 6 data rows plus 2 label rows printed and written.
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: p.451: the authors quote apparent molecular weights of CO2 of 44.295, 44.216 and 44.182 at 0, 25 and 40 C (0.65, 0.47, 0.39 % above 44.01); an ideal-gas conversion of S (mL STP per g water) to moles therefore underestimates real CO2 moles by up to about 0.6 %.
